2608.30853.title: Linguistic Distance Segregates Latent Representations in Automatic Speech Recognition Systems
2608.30853.paper_summary: While automatic speech recognition (ASR) models have achieved remarkable improvements in recent years, performance disparities persist across different speaker populations. One such disparity is for speakers whose first languages (L1) are from families distant from English. This paper investigates the relationship between first language background and English ASR performance. Through empirical analysis, we observe that the correlation between speakers' L1 distance and ASR error rates yields a systematic effect on English Speech, with its strength varying across datasets and models. This association is statistically significant in a follow-up analysis accounting for dataset-level variation in Tweedie mixed-effects models ($p<0.001$ across evaluated models). In addition, analysis of the latent space reveals a L1-based spatial segregation across deeper acoustic layers in the majority of evaluated architectures
2608.30853.paper_summary_zh: 儘管自動語音識別（ASR）模型在近年來取得了顯著的進步，但不同說話者群體之間的表現差異仍然存在。<lb/>其中一種差異是對於母語（L1）來自與英語相距較遠的語言家族的說話者。<lb/>本文探討了母語背景與英語 ASR 表現之間的關係。<lb/>通過實證分析，我們觀察到說話者的 L1 距離與 ASR 錯誤率之間的相關性對英語語音產生了系統性的影響，其強度在不同數據集和模型中有所變化。<lb/>在隨後的分析中，這種關聯在考慮到數據集層級變異的 Tweedie 混合效應模型中具有統計顯著性（$p<0.001$ 在評估的模型中）。<lb/>此外，潛在空間的分析顯示，在大多數評估的架構中，基於 L1 的空間隔離出現在較深的聲學層中。
